action: Operators of MONAI Label: apply the maintainers' fix and keep the server off the open internet; Cryptopolitan says a GitHub advisory dated 18 November 2026 rates the flaw critical (advisory page not read).
date_note: Date is the article's publication day (Cryptopolitan, 20 Nov 2026); Amazon says the activity ran from about 8 September and was detected on 10 September 2026. Amazon's own post was not readable, so its date is unknown.
exec: Amazon says AI agents run by an attacker found and exploited an unknown flaw in open-source software without human help, which it says shortens defenders' response time.
plain: Amazon says an attacker's AI agents found a previously unknown flaw in a medical-imaging program and used it to take over a university server. It says defenders should automate their responses.

sources.name: The Defiant (headline and standfirst only; article body did not load)

summary: Cryptopolitan reports that Amazon Threat Intelligence says AI agents coordinated through the open-source Cairn platform found and exploited a zero-day, which Amazon judged with high confidence, in MONAI Label, via a file-upload path traversal. Targeting of IPs tied to East Asian universities began around 8 September; Amazon detected it on 10 September. Amazon links the operator to China with moderate confidence.
title: Amazon says AI agents found and exploited a zero-day in MONAI Label

validation.note: Only Cryptopolitan was read in full; The Defiant's standfirst states the same core claim (CJ Moses, agents took over a university server) but its body did not load. Amazon's own post (aws.amazon.com security blog) and the GitHub advisory could not be read (page truncated, 403). Kept single_source.
